feedback: Written before this candidate has raced, so it states no outcome for it. The candidate is the iteration 1 and 6 baseline (kp 2.0, kd 0.2, ki 0, last_direction, weights -2..2, sensors x -0.02..0.02 at y 0.04, sensor_size 0.012, geometry unchanged) with base_speed raised from 1.4 to 1.5. The baseline is the best raced design (75.97), and iteration 6 reproduced it exactly, so it is a reliable comparison. Speed has only been lowered so far: iteration 2 cut base_speed to 1.2 but also set kd to 0.1, so the speed effect was never isolated. Iteration 2 lost s-bend progress (0.29 to 0.155) and oval progress (0.16 to 0.10), and the kd 0.1 runs in iteration 3 show that kd alone cost much of that, so the speed effect is still unclear. Raising speed is the one untested lever that bears on completion_time, since the 3.0 s limit needs about 1.5 m/s average. The candidate is a valid single-lever change. Read the race in this order. (1) If s-bend progress stays at or above 0.29 and line_loss_events and max_error do not rise, keep base_speed 1.5 and try a further small step only if completion appears. (2) If s-bend progress falls below about 0.22 with max_error near 0.06 to 0.065, speed is limiting the tightest bend, so return base_speed to 1.4. (3) If progress holds but max_error rises above 0.065, return to 1.4, since that means the robot is leaving the line sooner. In every case, kp and kd stay at 2.0 and 0.2 until the race shows a reason to change them. Approving this test is reasonable: the iteration budget is limited, and a single-lever speed test on the best baseline is the most informative race left.
requested_changes: If s-bend progress stays at or above 0.29 and line_loss_events on the s-bend and slalom do not rise above 1.95 and 2.0, keep base_speed 1.5 and try 1.6 in one step, since no run has yet finished and the 3 s limit needs about 1.5 m/s.
